findings: Opposite command signs are needed for both hands to move down together
No-head-follow large path produced about 6 degrees of torso-relative-waist appearance change
Head follow +20 us did not improve the large path; +40 us reduced relative appearance tilt to about 3 degrees in the comparison
Whole-body translation remains; head yaw compensation does not control vertical body position
Three consecutive selected round trips were performed and dual views reviewed
Operator observed one arm staying extended; synchronized commands have not yet established satisfactory bilateral elbow articulation
limitations: Image texture rotation is not an anatomical joint angle; angular search is quantized at 3 degrees
